pairs: Cum autem implesset omnia verba sua in aures plebis,
And when he had completed all his words in the hearing of the people,
Centurionis autem cujusdam servus male habens,
Now the servant of a certain centurion was dying,
And he was very dear to him.
And when he had heard about Jesus,
he sent elders of the Jews to him,
so that he would come and heal his servant.
At illi cum venissent ad Jesum,
And when they had come to Jesus,
Quia dignus est ut hoc illi præstes:
“He is worthy that you should provide this to him.
and he has built a synagogue for us.”
Et cum jam non longe esset a domo,
And when he was now not far from the house,
the centurion sent friends to him,
non enim sum dignus ut sub tectum meum intres:
For I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof.
et meipsum non sum dignum arbitratus ut venirem ad te:
I also did not consider myself worthy to come to you.
and my servant shall be healed.
Nam et ego homo sum sub potestate constitutus,
For I also am a man placed under authority,
And upon hearing this, Jesus was amazed.
And turning to the multitude following him,
nec in Israël tantam fidem inveni.
not even in Israel have I found such great faith.”
And those who had been sent,
who had been sick, was now healthy.
Et factum est: deinceps ibat in civitatem quæ vocatur Naim:
And it happened afterwards that he went to a city, which is called Nain.
et ibant cum eo discipuli ejus et turba copiosa.
And his disciples, and an abundant crowd, went with him.
Then, when he had drawn near to the gate of the city, behold,
ecce defunctus efferebatur filius unicus matris suæ:
a deceased person was being carried out, the only son of his mother,
et turba civitatis multa cum illa.
And a large crowd from the city was with her.
And when the Lord had seen her,
being moved by mercy over her,
And he drew near and touched the coffin.
Then those who carried it stood still.
And the dead youth sat up
And he gave him to his mother.
Then fear fell over all of them.
Quia propheta magnus surrexit in nobis:
“For a great prophet has risen up among us,”
et quia Deus visitavit plebem suam.
and, “For God has visited his people.”
Et exiit hic sermo in universam Judæam de eo,
And this word about him went out to all of Judea
and to the entire surrounding region.
Et nuntiaverunt Joanni discipuli ejus de omnibus his.
And the disciples of John reported to him concerning all these things.
Et convocavit duos de discipulis suis Joannes,
And John called two of his disciples,
and he sent them to Jesus,
“Are you he who is to come,
or should we wait for another?”
Cum autem venissent ad eum viri,
But when the men had come to him,
Joannes Baptista misit nos ad te dicens:
“John the Baptist has sent us to you, saying:
‘Are you he who is to come,
or should we wait for another?’”
(In ipsa autem hora multos curavit a languoribus,
he cured many of their diseases and wounds and evil spirits;
and to many of the blind,
Euntes renuntiate Joanni quæ audistis et vidistis:
“Go and report to John what you have heard and seen:
et beatus est quicumque non fuerit scandalizatus in me.
And blessed is anyone who has not taken offense at me.”
And when the messengers of John had withdrawn,
cœpit de Joanne dicere ad turbas:
he began to speak about John to the crowds.
“What did you go out to the desert to see?
A reed shaken by the wind?
Then what did you go out to see?
A man clothed in soft garments?
Ecce qui in veste pretiosa sunt et deliciis,
those who are in costly apparel and finery are in the houses of kings.
Then what did you go out to see?
This is he of whom it is written:
Ecce mitto angelum meum ante faciem tuam,
I send my Angel before your face,
qui præparabit viam tuam ante te.
who shall prepare your way before you.”
major inter natos mulierum propheta Joanne Baptista nemo est:
qui autem minor est in regno Dei,
no one is greater than the prophet John the Baptist.
But he who is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”
Et omnis populus audiens et publicani,
all the people and the tax collectors justified God,
by being baptized with the baptism of John.
Pharisæi autem et legisperiti consilium Dei spreverunt in semetipsos,
But the Pharisees and the experts in the law despised the counsel of God concerning themselves,
by not being baptized by him.
Cui ergo similes dicam homines generationis hujus?
“Therefore, to what shall I compare the men of this generation?
And to what are they similar?
Similes sunt pueris sedentibus in foro,
They are like children sitting in the marketplace,
a voracious man and a drinker of wine,
a friend of tax collectors and of sinners.’
Et justificata est sapientia ab omnibus filiis suis.
But wisdom is justified by all her children.”
Rogabat autem illum quidam de pharisæis ut manducaret cum illo.
Then certain Pharisees petitioned him, so that they might eat with him.
And he went into the house of the Pharisee, and he reclined at table.
a woman who was in the city, a sinner,
ut cognovit quod accubuisset in domo pharisæi,
found out that he was reclining at table in the house of the Pharisee,
so she brought an alabaster container of ointment.
et stans retro secus pedes ejus,
And standing behind him, beside his feet,
she began to wash his feet with tears,
and she wiped them with the hair of her head,
et osculabatur pedes ejus, et unguento ungebat.
and she kissed his feet, and she anointed them with ointment.
Then the Pharisee, who had invited him,
“This man, if he were a prophet,
sciret utique quæ et qualis est mulier,
would certainly know who and what kind of woman is this,
I have something to say to you.”
And since they did not have the ability to repay him,
So then, which of them loves him more?”
Æstimo quia is cui plus donavit.
“I suppose that it is he to whom he forgave the most.”
At ille dixit ei: Recte judicasti.
And he said to him, “You have judged correctly.”
You gave me no water for my feet.
hæc autem lacrimis rigavit pedes meos,
But she has washed my feet with tears,
and has wiped them with her hair.
You gave no kiss to me. But she,
from the time that she entered,
has not ceased to kiss my feet.
You did not anoint my head with oil.
hæc autem unguento unxit pedes meos.
But she has anointed my feet with ointment.
Because of this, I tell you:
But he who is forgiven less,
And those who sat at table with him began to say within themselves,
Quis est hic qui etiam peccata dimittit?
Then he said to the woman:
